correctness.rationale: The exact normalized Hardy overlap forces collinear kernel points and yields precisely two Möbius branches. At each radius the minus branch and aligned phase dominate. The global scalar inequality has an explicitly expanded nonnegative square with unique zero r=(a+k)/(1+ak+qb), which lies inside the disk for all a<1 and \(0<q\le1\). Direct rank-one norm and Cauchy–Schwarz chord calculations establish the unique saturation parameter, the exact squared-distance defect, and full boundary range. All endpoints and zero-symbol degeneracies are handled. The extracted standard-library checker reproduced 41,440 finite diagnostic assertions; these are supplementary to the written analytic all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The exact two-variable q-Berezin formula, maximizing normalized kernel pair, sharp norm-saturation locus, chordal defect and global constant-symbol range were not identified in the inspected primary sources or semantic research results. Bhattacharya–Patra Theorem 2.2 gives the kernel-pair parametrization and Section 3.4 covers the \(c=0\) case via linear symbol xi z, which are explicitly acknowledged as prior; neither implies the nonzero constant-symbol formula without solving a different optimization. General rank-one q-numerical bounds optimize over arbitrary unit vectors and cannot be used as equality formulas for the smaller prescribed Szego-kernel set. Earlier equivalent descriptions remain a real priority risk.

value.rationale: The result provides a complete sharp quantitative classification of the canonical nontrivial rank-one family of Hardy composition operators under a recently defined kernel-constrained q-Berezin invariant. Its nonzero-symbol two-parameter profile, unique extremizers, q-dependent norm-saturation curve, exact stability defect and sharp bounded universal range despite operator norms diverging at the disk boundary identify useful geometry absent from the previously treated origin endpoint. Exact natural complete classifications need not yield a general downstream theorem; no arbitrary parameter slice or routine table recomputation is claimed.
